title: py32-hal's half-duplex UART write turns the receiver off and never turns it back on, so a reader that is already waiting stops receiving.
summary: On 2026-07-15 embassy (commit 082d3b8a) changed UartTx::write and blocking_write so that, in half-duplex mode, they wait for the transmission to finish and then re-enable the receiver (RE) and disable the transmitter (TE). py32-hal, whose USART driver is copied from embassy, still clears RE at the start of every half-duplex write and leaves it to the next read() call to turn it back on; its ring-buffered reader never turns it back on. If the TX and RX halves of a split half-duplex Uart run in separate tasks, a reader that is already waiting never sees data again after the first write, so the receive side stops for good. The fix uses only functions and register fields that py32-hal already has (flush, blocking_flush, CR3.HDSEL, CR1.RE/TE).
